relationships.subject: high-fat diet
relationships.evidence_quote: rats fed an HFD for eight weeks presented greater neurological and motor coordination impairments than did rats fed a healthy diet

key_findings: 8-week HFD in rats caused metabolic syndrome features, mechanical allodynia, impaired rotarod performance, increased Evans dye penetration in cerebellum, hippocampus and hypothalamus, and endothelial thinning.
No direct causal link between BBB dysfunction and sensory-motor changes was shown.
